caption:
A <form> with no method attribute sends its data with GET. GET puts every field in the URL, password included. URLs end up in browser history, server logs and analytics tools.

Usually JavaScript intercepts the submit, so you never notice. But if your script fails to load or throws before preventDefault runs, the browser does the default.

The fix is one attribute: method="post" on the form. Add it even when JavaScript handles the submit.

Source: MDN, The Form element (method attribute).
